text:
<meta>The text is a section of the Prajnaparamita Sutra, specifically focusing on the purity of the "seer" in relation to the twelve links of dependent origination and the six perfections. The Tibetan orthography contains archaic features such as the reversed 'i' (gi-gu) and the use of 'm' as a prefix/suffix (e.g., myed for med), typical of early manuscript styles.</meta>

Because the six <term>ayatana</term> <gloss>sense sources</gloss> are completely pure, the seer is completely pure. Thus, the complete purity of the seer and the complete purity of the six sense sources are non-dual; they cannot be divided into two, they are not separate, and they are not distinct. Because the seer is completely pure, <term>sparsha</term> <gloss>contact</gloss> is completely pure. Because contact is completely pure, the seer is completely pure. Thus, the complete purity of the seer and the complete purity of contact are non-dual; they cannot be divided into two, they are not separate, and they are not distinct.

Because the seer is completely pure, <term>vedana</term> <gloss>feeling</gloss> is completely pure. Because feeling is completely pure, the seer is completely pure. Thus, the complete purity of the seer and the complete purity of feeling <note>the text repeats "thus the seer is completely pure" due to a scribal duplication</note> are non-dual.

Because of this, <term>trishna</term> <gloss>craving</gloss> is completely pure. Because craving is completely pure, and because the seer is completely pure, <term>upadana</term> <gloss>grasping</gloss> is completely pure. Because grasping is completely pure, the complete purity of grasping and craving are non-dual; they cannot be divided into two, they are not separate, and they are not distinct.

Because the seer is completely pure, grasping is completely pure. Because grasping is completely pure, the seer is completely pure. Thus, the complete purity of the seer and the complete purity of grasping are non-dual; they cannot be divided into two, they are not separate, and they are not distinct.

Because the seer is completely pure, <term>bhava</term> <gloss>becoming/existence</gloss> is completely pure. Because becoming is completely pure, they are non-dual; they cannot be divided into two, they are not separate, and they are not distinct.

The complete purity of the seer and the complete purity of the <term>paramita</term> <gloss>perfection</gloss> of patience <note>Sanskrit: kshanti</note> are linked. Because the perfection of patience is completely pure, the seer is completely pure. Thus, the complete purity of the seer and the complete purity of the perfection of patience are non-dual; they cannot be divided into two, they are not separate, and they are not distinct.

Because the seer is completely pure, the perfection of diligence <note>Sanskrit: virya</note> is completely pure. These are non-dual; they cannot be divided into two, they are not separate, and they are not distinct. Because the seer is completely pure, the seer is completely pure <note>this appears to be a repetitive formulaic reinforcement in the manuscript</note>. Thus, the complete purity of the seer and the complete purity of the perfection of diligence are non-dual.

The seer is completely pure. Thus, the seer is completely pure; thus, they are not distinct. Because the seer is completely pure, the perfection of concentration <note>Sanskrit: dhyana</note> is completely pure. Because of the one who has the complete purity of the perfection of concentration, the seer is completely pure. Thus, because the seer is completely pure, the perfection of wisdom <note>Sanskrit: prajna</note> is completely pure. The complete purity of the perfection of concentration is non-dual; it cannot be divided into two, it is not separate, and it is not distinct. Because the seer is completely pure, thus the seeing is completely pure.

<summary>This page discusses the ontological non-duality between the subject (the seer) and various factors of existence and Buddhist practice, asserting that all are equally pure in their essential nature. It applies this logic to the links of dependent origination like contact and craving, as well as the perfections of patience, diligence, and concentration.</summary>
<keywords>non-duality, purity, seer, sense sources, contact, craving, grasping, patience, diligence, concentration, Prajnaparamita</keywords>
